title: Ask for ten options, then remix
principle: Ask for many options; most won’t be good, and that’s fine—one or two will be. Then remix: pick favorites and ask for riffs that combine them. Claude creates options and starting points so you don’t stare at a blank canvas; you choose what’s good alone or as a combination of versions.
procedure: Ask for a large batch (e.g. ten) with deliberate variation.
Expect most to miss; keep one or two.
Name what works across favorites (layout from B, type from D).
Ask for several riffs that combine those pieces; repeat if needed.
Use volume specifically when collecting colleague feedback on flows.
examplePrompts: Give me 10 distinct options for this brief. Vary layout, hierarchy, and visual language. I will pick; do not optimize for a single “best” answer.
I like option B and a little of option D. Give me five riffs that smoosh those together.
Generate 10 distinct layout directions for this brief (one sentence each + thumbnail description). Do not polish. Then remix the best 2 into a hybrid and explain what you took from each.
tips: Volume is intentional: most options can fail if a few succeed.
Remix across versions instead of polishing one weak default.
Nate also generates many flow versions specifically to collect colleague feedback.

antiPatterns: Polishing one weak default instead of sampling.
Skipping this step and hoping vibes carry the craft.
checklist: Batch size is large enough to explore.
Feedback round uses multiple flow versions when needed.
Fresh pass confirms the prompt constraints were followed.
promptWhy: Volume + explicit “I will pick” stops single-answer collapse.
Named remix targets turn selection into a generative step.
Volume before polish escapes local maxima; remix forces intentional combination.

stateRequirements.responsive: Check 390px and desktop plus 200% zoom; preserve reading order, wrap long text and keep actions reachable.
stateRequirements.accessibility: Use semantic headings and native controls, visible labels and focus; normal text contrast at least 4.5:1.
stateRequirements.keyboard: Complete the primary action using Tab, Shift+Tab, Enter and Space; no pointer-only information or focus trap.
stateRequirements.reducedMotion: Remove nonessential movement; preserve all state and information without waiting for animation.
stateRequirements.loading: Show pending feedback only during real work; retain context and allow navigation away.
stateRequirements.empty: Distinguish no content from no matching results; explain how to proceed or reset filters.
stateRequirements.error: Explain the failed action, retain user input and offer recovery; never claim success on failure.
stateRequirements.interruption: A newer action wins; cancel or ignore stale results and keep controls responsive.
stateRequirements.stateChange: Announce important results politely without moving focus unexpectedly.

compatibility.rule: Start with one technique. Add at most one companion for a distinct unsolved problem; candidates are suggestions, not verified compatibility.
conflicts: Two techniques changing the same visual role require an explicit winner.
Do not combine multiple entrance or attention effects on one target.
Aesthetic subtraction must not remove semantics, feedback or attribution.
compatibility.stop: Stop when the named task is clearer and acceptance evidence is recorded; do not add polish without a problem.
